stories.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the measures as "common-sense tools that do not divide but really help to integrate".
stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, Vincenzo Nuzzolese/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images By Davide Ghiglione in Rome Published 1 hour ago The Italian government has approved a ban on the burqa and niqab in schools, along with a limit on the share of pupils who speak little Italian in any one class. A 30% cap will be imposed on children without Italian citizenship or poor knowledge of the Italian language in the first year of primary, middle and high school. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the measures as "common-sense tools that do not divide but really help to integrate". Opposition parties accuse the government of pandering to the policies of the hard-right Futuro Nazionale party, ahead of a general election next year. Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara has said the limit is "purely linguistic" rather than one of citizenship, while he has sought to frame the ban on the niqab and burqa as a matter of gender equality.
